1 498(A), 323 of IPC.& Sec. 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
 2.
The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Smt.Anitha T..

The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused got married complainant on 30-01-2002 at Sri Maruthi Hanumanthappa Kalyana Mantap,
Hosakerehalli.
At the time of marriage, as per the demand of the accused, the parents of complainant i.e. CW 2 and CW 3 had given Rs.45,000/- in cash and a gold neck chain as dowry to the accused.

After the marriage, when complainant was residing with accused at Ittamadu, Bangalore, accused used to abuse complainant in foul and filthy language and was ill-treating her by saying that her parents have not given him sufficient dowry and forced her to bring additional dowry of Rs.Two lakhs and assaulted her.

In this regard, the complainant had filed first information statement before Basavanagudi Women P.S. and the same was registered in crime No.72/2006 against the accused for the offences U/s.498A, 323 of I.P.C. & Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
In the said case the accused and complainant had compromised the matter.

Thereafter, when complainant and accused were residing at  3  C.C.No.23833/2015 Subramanyapura, Bangalore, accused used to abuse complainant by saying that she is a prostitute and during night times he used to strangulate her neck and assault her by holding her hair and used to kick her on to her stomach and also used to tell his children to call complainant as prostitute.

Based on the said information of Smt.Anitha, a case in Cr.No.48/2015 came to be registered against Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
2 the accused for the offences punishable U/s.498(A) , 323 of IPC. &
Sec. 3 & 4 Dowry Prohibition Act.
 3.
After completion of the investigation, the Police Inspector of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and was enlarged on bail.

The prosecution papers was furnished to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.
 4.
Before framing charge an opportunity of being heard was provided to the accused and the prosecution.

After hearing both the sides and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offence was framed against accused and same was read over to the accused in the language known to him, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The plea of the  4  C.C.No.23833/2015 accused was recorded.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution got examined PW-1 to PW-7 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4 documents.
The Statement of Accused as required U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded.
The accused denied the incriminating materials appearing against him.
The accused got examined one witness by name Hemantharaju as DW-1 and no documents are marked on his behalf.
6. Heard arguments on both sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
3  7. The following points arise for my determination:-
1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the complainant and accused got married on  30-01-2002 at Sri Maruthi Hanumanthappa Kalyana  Mantap, Hosakerehalli.

At the time of marriage, as per  the demand of the accused, the parents of complainant  i.e. CW 2 and CW 3 had given Rs.45,000/- in cash and a  gold neck chain as dowry to the accused and thereby  accused has committed offence punisahble u/s.3 & 4 of  DP. Act?

2) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that after the marriage, when complainant was  residing with accused at Ittamadu, Bangalore, accused  used to abuse complainant in foul and filthy language  and was ill-treating her by saying that her parents have  not given him sufficient dowry and forced her to bring  additional dowry of Rs.Two lakhs and assaulted her.
 5  C.C.No.23833/2015  Thereafter, when complainant and accused were residing  at Subramanyapura, Bangalore accused used to abuse  complainant by saying that she is a prostitute and  during night times he used to strangulate her neck and  assault her by holding her hair and used to kick her on  to her stomach and also used to tell his children to call  complainant as prostitute and caused mental and  physical cruelty to the complainant and also caused  simple injury and thereby accused has committed  offences punishable U/s.498A and 323 of I.P.C?
 3) what order?
 8.

My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 and 2........In the Negative.
 Point No.3........

As per final order, for the following:
 R E A SON S  9. POINT No.1:-
It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused
, the prosecution got examined PW-1 to PW-7.

PW-1 Smt.
Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
4

Anitha is the first informant/complainant, PW-2 Thyagaraj is the father of complainant, PW-3 Umadevi is the mother of complainant, PW-4 Venkatesh and PW-5 Rekha are the panch witnesses to the Ex.P.2 spot panchanama.
PW-6 Dr.Mohan is the Doctor working at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital,Bangalore and he has treated complainant.
PW-7 Kavtiha is the Investigating Officer.
The prosecution got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4 documents.
6  C.C.No.23833/2015 Ex.P.1 is the first information statement, Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.3 is the wound certificate.
Ex.P.4 is the FIR.
10.The
learned Sr.APP vehemently argued that the prosecution has examined PW.1 to PW.3.

Out of them, PW-1 is the victim and PW-2 and 3 are the parents of PW-1 and they have supported the case of prosecution and argued the accused has not disputed the marriage and nothing worth is elicited by the accused from PW 1 to 3 to disprove the case of the prosecution and also argued to prove the injuries, the prosecution has examined PW-6 Doctor and has examined PW-4 and PW-5 to prove Ex.P.2 panchanama and has elicited material answers from DW-1 to prove that there was a quarrel between complainant and accused and sought to convict the accused.
 11.

Per Contra, the learned counsel for the accused stoutly argued that the prosecution has failed to place material before the court to establish that accused had demanded dowry and PW2 had given dowry to the accused and argued there is a delay in lodging the first information statement and the delay is not properly explained and argued complainant has not narrated the Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
5 injuries sustained by her and argued there is a contradiction in the testimony of PW 1 to 3 and argued Ex.P.3 wound certificate is a  7  C.C.No.23833/2015 created document and the complainant in her cross examination has deposed that she signed at Ex.P.2 spot panchanama in the police station and argued the earlier case filed by complainant against accused ended in compromise and once again the complainant has made the very same allegation at Ex.P.1 first information statement and sought for acquittal of the accused.
 12.

On considering the arguments addressed by the learned Sr.APP and the learned counsel for the accused and on perusal of Ex.P.1 first information statement, complainant/PW-1 has stated that, marriage between her and accused was performed on 30-01- 2002.

It is required to be noted that the prosecution has examined PW-7 Kavitha and she is the Investigating officer and she in her examination in chief has deposed that PW-1/complainant provided marriage photos and marriage invitation card along with first information statement.
The said documents are not marked.

Even otherwise, on careful scrutiny of the cross examination of prosecution witnesses by the accused coupled with testimony of DW-1, it depicts that the accused has not disputed the relationship between himself and the complainant and he has also not disputed the marriage between himself and the complainant.
In this background now I enter into the domain of oral and  8  C.C.No.23833/2015 documentary evidence let in by the prosecution and accused.

The Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
6 allegation as against accused made by the complainant/prosecution and the defence set up by the accused can be categorized into four folds.
Let me discuss each and every aspect in detail.

I) Demand of dowry:
 13.
It is to be noted that at Ex.P.1 first information statement, the complainant has stated that an amount of Rs.45,000/- in cash and a gold neck chain was given to the accused.

During examination-in-chief, PW-1 and 3 have deposed that as per the demand of the accused an amount of Rs.45,000/-
in cash and a gold neck chain was given to the accused as dowry.
PW-2 in his examination in chief deposed that at the time of marriage, an amount of Rs.40,000/- in cash and a gold neck chain was given to the accused as dowry.

During cross examination,
PW-1 deposed that her father was working as attender at Sheshadripuram college and she has deposed that her father has five children including her.
The accused has suggested to PW-1 that her father was not having financial capacity to provide education to his children.
PW-1 denied the said suggestion and voluntarily deposed that her mother was selling flowers.
PW-1  9  C.C.No.23833/2015 denied the suggestion put forth by the accused that the income earned by her father and mother was only sufficient to provide food and paying rent to the house.

PW-1 denied that she has not mentioned at Ex.P.1 that accused had demanded Rs.45,000/-
cash and gold neck chain.

It is worth to note that at Ex.P.1, the complainant/PW1 has not mentioned that accused demanded Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
7 Rs.45,000/- in cash and gold neck chain as dowry.
 14.

Be that as it may, PW-1 deposed that Rs.45,000/- was given to the accused and gold neck chain was given to the accused on the date of marriage and also deposed the bill for having purchased gold neck chain is not with her and deposed when gold neck chain was put on the accused, photo was taken and the same is with her and she will produce the same before the court.
It is to be noted that the prosecution or the complainant/PW1 has not produced the said photo before the court. PW-2
in his cross examination admitted that from the salary he used to earn, it was sufficient for providing education and food to the children.
PW-2 admitted that he has no receipt/bill pertaining to gold neck chain and he has deposed that he has given dowry of Rs.45,000/-cash to the accused from the money which he had with him.
PW-2 denied  10  C.C.No.23833/2015 the suggestion that accused did not demand dowry and that he has not given dowry to the accused.
PW-3 in her cross examination deposed that she was doing flower business and denied that no cash and gold ornament was given to the accused.

15 . It is pertinent to note that either the complainant or prosecution have not placed any material before the court to establish that PW-2 had Rs.45,000/-cash with him on the date of marriage of complainant and accused or prior to that date and no receipt/bill has been produced by the prosecution to establish that gold neck chain was purchased by PW-2 and was given to the Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
8 accused as dowry.
That apart, as discussed there is no narration in the Ex.P.1 first information statement that accused had demanded dowry of Rs.45,000/-cash and gold neck chain from PW-2 and PW-3.

As such, it could be concluded that the allegation of the complainant/ prosecution in respect of demand of dowry by the accused and payment of Rs.45,000/- in cash by PW-2 and giving gold neck chain gets dislodged.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

POINT No.2 :- II) ALLEGATION WITH RESPECT TO CAUSING MENTAL AND PHYSICAL CRUELTY AND ASSAULT ON THE COMPLAINANT BY THE ACCUSED :
 11  C.C.No.23833/2015  16.
It is to be noted that it is the case of prosecution that after the marriage, accused used to assault and strangulate her neck every now and then in demand of dowry of Rs.Two lakhs.

At Ex.P.1 PW-1 has stated that on 19-12-2006 accused assaulted her and caused mental cruelty and in this regard, she had lodged complaint before the police and thereafter on 27-08-2008 accused told before the court that he would not torture her and took her back to the matrimonial house.

During examination in chief, PW-1 has deposed that after the marriage, when she was residing with the accused at Ittamadu, accused used to harass her, assault her,
strangulate her neck and used to abuse her and her parents in foul and filthy language and he was forcing her to bring dowry of Rs.Two lakhs.

PW-1 has also deposed that on 19-12-2006 she had lodged complaint before the police and before the mediation center and in the family court, the accused promised her that he would take care her well and deposed the said case got closed.

PW 2 Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
9 and 3 have also deposed in their examination in chief about the same.
During cross examination PW-2 and PW-3 have admitted that both complainant and accused have compromised in the earlier case filed by the complainant against the accused.
Both PW 2 and 3 have also admitted that upto 2015 complainant and  12  C.C.No.23833/2015 accused had cordial relationship.
PW-1 also in her cross examination admitted that she had compromised with the accused in the earlier criminal case filed by her against the accused.
17. It is to be noted that at Ex.P.1, the complainant has once again narrated about the previous ill treatment meted out to her by the accused in demand of dowry.

As complainant and accused have compromised the matter in the earlier criminal case filed by the complainant against accused which was registered in Crime No.72/2006 of Basavanagudi Women P.S., this court is of the view that the complainant is debarred from re-opening the earlier allegations made in the Cr.No.72/2006.

That apart, PW-2 and 3 have specifically admitted that complainant and accused had cordial relationship upto 2015 and PW-1 in her cross examination had admitted that after she going back to matrimonial house, she delivered second child.

Therefore, as discussed as the matter between the complainant and accused was compromised, once again complainant cannot prosecute accused on the same allegations made in crime No.72/2006 as it amounts to waiver.

18 . It is to be noted that at Ex.P.1 the complainant has alleged that after settlement in the earlier case she was residing Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
10 with the accused at Goudanapalaya and in the said house accused  13  C.C.No.23833/2015 used to call her prostitute and used to kick her, strangulate her neck, abuse her and was instigating his children to call the complainant as prostitute and used to tell complainant everyday to fall from the house and die.

It is also alleged that on 26-03-2015 from 1-00 a.m. to morning hours, accused assaulted her with club and on the next day she intelligently came out of the house, locked the house and went to her paternal house.
PW-2 and 3 in their examination in chief have deposed that accused assaulted complainant and drove her out of the house.
PW-2 deposed that the said incident occurred in the year 2015.
Whereas PW-3 deposed that the said incident occurred on 27-03-2015.
Both PW 2 and PW3 have deposed that complainant was provided treatment at Bowring & Ladycurzon hospital.

PW-1 in her examination in chief has deposed that on 26-03-2015 when she called accused and informed that her son is not keeping well, accused came home and assaulted her with club and on the next day morning also the accused assaulted her with club and deposed she went to her paternal house and took treatment at Gowdanapalya hospital.
19. During cross examination PW-1 admitted that she has not taken treatment in any hospital as inpatient.
Though PW-1 in her examination in chief deposed that she took treatment at  14  C.C.No.23833/2015 Gowdanapalya hospital, the prosecution has not produced any medical record to establish the same.

It is interesting to note that PW-1 has no where deposed that she took treatment at Bowring Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
11 and Ladycurzon hospital.

sentences.text: That apart, PW-1 in her cross examination, admitted that when her husband/accused assaulted her and strangulated her neck she has not taken treatment.

It is worth to note that PW-2 and PW-3 specifically admitted that "

 20.

Be that as it may it is required to be noted that the prosecution has examined PW-6 Dr.Mohan and he in his examination in chief deposed that on 28-03-2015 at about 10-15 a.m., complainant came to him with the history of assault by her husband and on examination, he found injuries mentioned at Ex.P.3 wound certificate and he has reported that the said injuries are simple in nature and deposed if a person assaults with hand and with nail, injury mentioned at Ex.P.3 can happen.
During cross examination PW-6 admitted that he has not mentioned in Ex.P.3 about injured being treated as in patient and deposed he has reported to the police about giving treatment to the injured.
15  C.C.No.23833/2015 PW-6 admitted he has not mentioned the age of the wound at Ex.P3 and also admitted he did not find any external injuries on the neck, head and stomach of the injured.
It is to be noted that nothing has been narrated by complainant/PW-1 in the Ex.P.1 about the injuries mentioned in Ex.P.3 and that she sustained the same on account of assault made by the accused.

As PW-1 herself has not deposed in her testimony about she having taken Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
12 treatment at Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital and also as she has not narrated about the injuries she sustained as mentioned in Ex.P.3 wound certificate, at Ex.P.1 first information statement and also as she has not mentioned in the Ex.P.3 or in her testimony about the date of she taking treatment at the said hospital, the testimony of PW6 and Ex.P.3 wound certificate is of no consequence as it lacks corroboration by PW-1 and the same is not helpful to the prosecution to bring home the guilt of the accused.
 21.
It is to be noted that the accused got his son Hemantharaju examined as DW-1.

DW-1 in his examination chief deposed that he was residing with his father, mother, grand mother and his brother at Gowdanapalaya house and deposed that his grand mother was sick and deposed in the year, 2015 during night hours his mother and father were quarreling with each other  16  C.C.No.23833/2015 in the matter of looking after his bed ridden grand mother and deposed that his mother was telling that she cannot look after his grand mother and on the next day morning she was outside the house and took his brother along with her and she called him and he did not go.
During cross examination, DW-1 deposed that his parents were quarreling with each other in the matter of his brother having fever.
Even PW-1 in her examination in chief deposed that accused assaulted her when she told accused over the phone that their son is having fever.

22. That apart, PW-1 in her cross examination deposed as on 25-03-2015 her elder son was aged 12 years and he was knowing Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
13 what was happening in the house.
Therefore, the testimony of DW1 and PW1 makes it clear that, PW-1 and accused were quarreling with each other in the house.
But the accused has taken a stand that PW-1 was not taking care of his ailing mother.
DW-1 in his examination in chief has also deposed that accused and PW-1 used to quarrel in the matter of taking care of his ailing grand mother.
During cross examination the accused has suggested to PW-2 and PW-3 that on 26-03-2015, the mother of the accused was bed ridden.
PW-2 and PW-3 pleaded ignorance about the same.
PW-2  17  C.C.No.23833/2015 and 3 denied that their daughter told accused that he cannot take care of her ailing mother in law and quarreled with accused and went out of the house.

That apart, PW-1 in her cross examination admitted that her mother in law used to be at home and also admitted that her mother in law was bed ridden and denied she did not take care of her mother-in-law between 2013 to 2015.

The said admission of PW-1 and the suggestion put forth by the accused to PW 2 and PW 3 coupled with testimony of DW-1 makes it clear that the mother of the accused was residing with accused and complainant and they both use to quarrel in the matter of taking care of ailing mother.
That apart, there is nothing on record to show that the second son of the complainant and accused had fever on 26-03-2015.
Therefore the motive for commission of offence by the accused on 26-03-2015 does not stand established by the prosecution.

23.That apart, nothing has been deposed by PW-1 or DW-1 Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
14
that accused used to call complainant as prostitute and that accused was instigating either DW-1 or the brother of DW-1 to call complainant as prostitute.

The prosecution has examined PW-7 Kavitha and she is the Investigating officer and she in her examination in chief has deposed about receiving Ex.P.1 first  18  C.C.No.23833/2015 information statement from the complainant and registration of Ex.P.4 FIR and drawing Ex.P.2 spot panchanama and recording statements of CW 2 and 3, obtaining ExP.3 wound certificate and filing of chargesheet against the accused.

During cross examination,PW-7 deposed she had submitted requisition to the doctor for providing wound certificate and admitted she has not produced requisition before the court and deposed when she enquired the neighbourers nobody co-operated.
It is to be noted that no independent witnesses have been examined by the PW-7 to establish the alleged incident.
24. It is to be noted that, as per the admission of PW2 and PW3 accused and complainant had cordial relationship upto 2015.
Notably, between 2008-2015 PW-1 and accused lived together and second child was born to them.
It is pertinent to note that, minor spats or occasional disagreements between spouses, typical in everyday life due to differences of opinion.
In the instant case PW1 and accused had difference of opinion in the matter of taking care of ailing mother of accused.
Therefore, this court is of the view that such difference of opinion between complainant and accused is not sufficient to establish offence U/s498(A) of IPC.

It must be noted that every harassment ordinarily would not attract offence Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
15  19  C.C.No.23833/2015 U/s.498A of IPC and to attract an offence U/s.498A IPC., it must be established that cruelty or harassment to wife was to compel her to fulfill illegal demand of dowry.
As discussed, at Ex.P.1 there is no such allegation made by the complainant, that accused was harassing complainant in demand of dowry from 2008 onwards upto the date of filing Ex.P.1.

In addition to that, as PW- 1/complainant has not narrated the motive of the accused for alleged crime committed on her on 26-03-2015 at Ex.P.1 and also as PW-7 has not recorded the statements of any independent witnesses and also as discussed, the testimony of PW-6 lacks corroboration from PW-1, it could be concluded that the prosecution has failed to prove alleged physical and mental cruelty meted out by the accused to the complainant in demand of dowry.

III SPOT PANCHANAMA:-
 25.
In order to prove place of occurrence, the prosecution has examined PW-4 Venkatesh and PW-5 Rekha.

PW-4 and PW-5 in their examination in chief identified their signature at Ex.P.2 spot panchanama and deposed on 13-05-2015 they signed at Ex.P.2 in the matter of accused giving torture to the complainant.
During cross examination both PW4 and PW5 admitted that police have not given notice to them for attending Ex.P.2 panchanama.
PW-5 in  20  C.C.No.23833/2015 her cross examination admitted that complainant is her relative.
It is to be noted that PW-1 in her cross examination deposed that she signed at Ex.P.2 panchanama in the police station.

On careful Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
16 scrutiny Ex.P.2 panchanama the same is drawn by PW-7 at No.16,
Dodda Gowdanapalya, Subramanyapura and notably, the same is drawn on 13-05-2015 at the instance of PW-1.

Though PW-4 and 5 supported the case of the prosecution in respect of Ex.P.2 spot panchanama, as admitted by them, no notic was issued to them by the Investigating officer calling upon them to take part in drawing Ex.P.2 spot panchanama.
Thar apart, PW-1 in her cross examination deposed that she signed at ExP.2 in the police station.
Therefore, the case of the prosecution in respect of drawing Ex.P.2 spot panchanama at the place of occurrence gets falsified.

As such,
it could be concluded that the prosecution has failed to prove Ex.P.2 spot panchanama.

IV. DELAY IN LODGING FIR:-
 26.
It is to be noted that as per the prosecution case alleged incident occurred on 26-03-2015 and notably, Ex.P.1 first information statement came to be lodged on 12-05-2015.
There is a delay of 47 days in lodging Ex.P.1 first information statement.
The complainant in her first information statement has stated that  21  C.C.No.23833/2015 after she taking treatment at Borwing hospital and after recovering from the same, she has lodged Ex.P.1.

As discussed and as per testimony of PW-6, PW-1 took treatment on 28-03-2015 and notably, PW-6 has opined that injury mentioned at Ex.P.3 wound certificate is simple in nature and PW-1 herself has no where deposed or stated in the Ex.P.1 as to what all injuries she sustained.
In my view PW-1 has failed to narrate the proper reason at Ex.P.1 for delay in lodging the Ex.P.1.

At this juncture, I find it Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
17 appropriate to quote the ruling decided between Harilal ETC Vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh in Crl.Appeal No.2216 and 2217/2011 by the Hon'ble Apex Court decided on 05-09-2023 wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court at para-19 has held that:-
When an FIR is delayed, in absence of proper explanation, the courts must be on guard and test the evidence meticulously to rule out possibility of embellishments in the prosecution story, in as much as delay gives opportunity for deliberation and guess work.

It is to be noted that in a ruling reported in 2012 AIR (Crl.)
page 190 decided between Kailash Gaur and others Vs. State of Assam.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, delay in lodging FIR  22  C.C.No.23833/2015 and if it is not explained satisfactorily by the prosecution, the same is fatal.

In the light of principle laid down above, this court is of the view that the delay in lodging the Ex.P.1 first information statement by the complainant against the accused is not satisfactorily explained by the prosecution.

27. On appreciation of entire materials placed on record by the prosecution and the accused, I am the considered view that there are material contradictions in the testimony of the witnesses examined by the prosecution and there is no corroboration of the facts alleged by the prosecution.

A bear perusal of Ex.P.1 First Information statement, it discloses that complainant was Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
18 assaulted by the accused by using club and notably, the said club has not been seized by the I.O., i.e. PW-7.

That apart Ex.P.1 First Information statement is bereft of any details like demand of dowry by the accused and there is no semblance of materials against accused to constitute an offence U/s.498A, 323 of I.P.C., and Sec.
3 & 4 of D.P.Act and also as there is a delay in lodging FIR, this Court is of the view that the prosecution has failed to bring home  23  C.C.No.23833/2015 guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in the Negative.
28. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused
, the prosecution got examined PW-1 to PW-7.
As complainant and accused have compromised the matter in the earlier criminal case filed by the complainant against accused which was registered in Crime No.72/2006 of Basavanagudi Women P.S., this court is of the view that the complainant is debarred from re-opening the earlier allegations made in the Cr.No.72/2006.
That apart, PW-2 and 3 have specifically admitted that complainant and accused had cordial relationship upto 2015 and PW-1 in her cross examination had admitted that after she going back to matrimonial house, she delivered second child.
Therefore, as discussed as the matter between the complainant and accused was compromised, once again complainant cannot prosecute accused on the same allegations made in crime No.72/2006 as it amounts to waiver.
The said admission of PW-1 and the suggestion put forth by the accused to PW 2 and PW 3 coupled with testimony of DW-1 makes it clear that the mother of the accused was residing with accused and complainant and they both use to quarrel in the matter of taking care of ailing mother.
That apart, there is nothing on record to show that the second son of the complainant and accused had fever on 26-03-2015.
Therefore the motive for commission of offence by the accused on 26-03-2015 does not stand established by the prosecution.
It is pertinent to note that, minor spats or occasional disagreements between spouses, typical in everyday life due to differences of opinion.
In the instant case PW1 and accused had difference of opinion in the matter of taking care of ailing mother of accused.
Therefore, this court is of the view that such difference of opinion between complainant and accused is not sufficient to establish offence U/s498(A) of IPC.
It must be noted that every harassment ordinarily would not attract offence Anitha T vs N Nataraj on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171345424/
15  19  C.C.No.23833/2015 U/s.498A of IPC and to attract an offence U/s.498A IPC., it must be established that cruelty or harassment to wife was to compel her to fulfill illegal demand of dowry.
As discussed, at Ex.P.1 there is no such allegation made by the complainant, that accused was harassing complainant in demand of dowry from 2008 onwards upto the date of filing Ex.P.1.
In addition to that, as PW- 1/complainant has not narrated the motive of the accused for alleged crime committed on her on 26-03-2015 at Ex.P.1 and also as PW-7 has not recorded the statements of any independent witnesses and also as discussed, the testimony of PW-6 lacks corroboration from PW-1, it could be concluded that the prosecution has failed to prove alleged physical and mental cruelty meted out by the accused to the complainant in demand of dowry.
In the light of principle laid down above, this court is of the view that the delay in lodging the Ex.P.1 first information statement by the complainant against the accused is not satisfactorily explained by the prosecution.
27. On appreciation of entire materials placed on record by the prosecution and the accused, I am the considered view that there are material contradictions in the testimony of the witnesses examined by the prosecution and there is no corroboration of the facts alleged by the prosecution.
That apart Ex.P.1 First Information statement is bereft of any details like demand of dowry by the accused and there is no semblance of materials against accused to constitute an offence U/s.498A, 323 of I.P.C., and Sec.
3 & 4 of D.P.Act and also as there is a delay in lodging FIR, this Court is of the view that the prosecution has failed to bring home  23  C.C.No.23833/2015 guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
